slides.main: Lactose intolerant? Most adults still tolerate a cup of milk at once.
slides.sub: How much lactose is usually fine, and which dairy foods have the least.

slides.main: Many people who think they are lactose intolerant digest lactose normally.
slides.sub: A US expert panel found this. A breath test that also records your symptoms can check.

slides.main: A review found most adults tolerate 12 to 15 g at once.
slides.sub: That is roughly one cup of milk. Taken with other food, up to 18 g is usually tolerated.

slides.main: Hard cheese has about 0.1 g of lactose per 100 g.
slides.sub: Whole milk has about 4.7 g. Yoghurt and cream cheese contain more than hard cheese.

slides.main: A strict lactose-free diet is usually not needed.
slides.sub: Cut down for a short time, then add dairy back slowly. Ask a GP or dietitian first.

slides.main: Get medical help if you have:
items: Blood in your stool or black stools
Symptoms that wake you up at night
Coeliac disease or IBD in your family
